In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of dietary fatty acids on the growth and development of the foetus.
the influence of maternal dietary fatty acids on the pathophysiology of intrauterine foetal growth and neonatal development.
the study of the effects of dietary lipids, especially polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) of the n-3 and n-6 families, on the growth and development of the foetus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fetus has the ability to metabolize and utilize some of the essential fatty acids and antioxidant vitamins transferred from the mother, and that these compounds are essential to support its development and protect it from the oxidative stress to which it will be submitted in the extrauterine environment.
the fatty acid composition of the mother's diet has a profound effect on the fatty acid profile of the fetus and the newborn.
, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, a diet rich in fish and fish oils, and in particular rich in DHA and EPA, is beneficial for the fetus and for the neonate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fetus is able to synthesize the fatty acids and liposoluble vitamins needed for its development, but the maternal diet can affect the amounts available.
the fetus is able to maintain its own fatty acid profile, which differs from that of the mother, and is able to synthesize the essential fatty acids and liposoluble vitamins from their precursors.
the fatty acid and vitamin status of the fetus is influenced by the mother's status, but also by the fetal capacity to metabolize these compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the placenta is not a passive barrier, but rather a selective filter that allows for transfer of nutrients and metabolites that are important for the developing fetus.
the fetus is not a passive recipient of maternal nutrients, but it is able to modify them in order to meet its needs.
a healthy diet is essential for the health of the mother and the baby.
